## Session outcome

Reconcile independent thermodynamic routes to K and then solve composition.

**Before class:** Review formation Gibbs energies, reaction enthalpy/entropy and integration of heat capacity.

## Reaction equilibrium changes composition

$$n_i=n_{i,0}+\nu_i\xi$$
$$\Delta_rG=\sum_i\nu_i\mu_i=\Delta_rG^\circ+RT\ln Q$$

Stoichiometric coefficients are negative for reactants and positive for products. At an interior equilibrium, ΔrG=0.

::: {.notes}
Start from differential G at fixed T,P. Feasible extent bounds follow nonnegative amounts; boundary equilibria need separate treatment.
:::

## K and Q have different roles

$$\ln K=-\frac{\Delta_rG^\circ}{RT},\qquad Q=\prod_i a_i^{\nu_i}$$

K is tied to T and the fixed reaction/standard-state convention. Q describes the supplied state.

Q=K is an equilibrium condition, not an identity for every measured composition.

::: {.notes}
Use the Lab 12 equilibrium-assertion control to emphasize evidence. Do not call −RTlnQ a standard Gibbs energy unless equilibrium is justified.
:::

## Standard states keep K dimensionless

| Phase | Activity used |
|---|---|
| Gas | φᵢ yᵢ P/p° |
| Solute, molarity standard | γᵢ cᵢ/c° |
| Liquid solution | γᵢ xᵢ |
| Present pure solid/liquid | 1 |

Formation data and activities must use matching phases and standards.

::: {.notes}
Discuss why a numerical Kp with pressure units is not automatically the same object as thermodynamic dimensionless K.
:::

## Several routes to standard Gibbs energy

1. Supplied ΔrG° at the evaluation T.
2. Formation properties: ΔrG°=ΣνᵢΔfGᵢ°.
3. Reaction enthalpy and entropy: ΔrG°=ΔrH°−TΔrS°.
4. Reference K with integrated temperature dependence.
5. Equilibrium activities, only when equilibrium is supported.

Independent inputs can disagree; the lab preserves the disagreement.

::: {.notes}
Use the six thermodynamic rows in Lab 12: constant-property and Cp variants create extra rows, not separate laws.
:::

## A reference-state check

Lab 12 synthetic A₂ ⇌ 2A at 350 K uses ΔrG°=−4.000 kJ/mol.

$$\ln K=\frac{4000}{R(350)}=1.37454,\qquad K\approx3.95326$$

With ΔrH°=50.000 kJ/mol and ΔrS°=54000/350 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the H−TS route gives the same value.

::: {.notes}
This is a synthetic thermodynamic definition, not a measured dissociation reaction. Ask students to verify the joule conversion and reference basis.
:::

## Constant-enthalpy van ’t Hoff relation

$$\frac{d\ln K}{dT}=\frac{\Delta_rH^\circ(T)}{RT^2}$$

With constant ΔrH° over the stated interval,
$$\ln\frac{K(T)}{K(T_r)}=\frac{\Delta_rH_r^\circ}{R}\left(\frac1{T_r}-\frac1T\right)$$

An endothermic reaction has increasing K with T in this approximation.

::: {.notes}
Derive integration signs on the board. A point value of ΔG° provides no temperature derivative.
:::

## Constant heat-capacity correction

$$\Delta_rH^\circ(T)=\Delta_rH_r^\circ+\Delta_rC_p^\circ(T-T_r)$$
$$\Delta_rS^\circ(T)=\Delta_rS_r^\circ+\Delta_rC_p^\circ\ln(T/T_r)$$

The integrated ln K adds
$$\frac{\Delta_rC_p^\circ}{R}\left[\ln(T/T_r)+T_r/T-1\right]$$

to the constant-enthalpy expression.

::: {.notes}
Use the written formula to compare with Lab 12. Discuss the validity interval, phase transitions and why constant Cp is still an approximation.
:::

## Reference consistency and temperature applicability

Changing only Kref while holding reference H and S fixed creates two independent anchors that may disagree.

Point ΔG° and formation-energy data are unavailable away from their supplied T unless an explicit temperature model exists.

Keeping ln K avoids false zeros or infinities from exponent underflow/overflow.

::: {.notes}
Ask whether apparent curve agreement at one T establishes agreement of derivatives. It does not.
:::

## Equilibrium extent and pressure

For a neutral ideal-gas reaction,
$$Q(\xi)=\prod_i\left[y_i(\xi)P/p^\circ\right]^{\nu_i}$$

Solve lnQ(ξ)−lnK=0 within nonnegative mole amounts. Pressure changes Q and equilibrium composition, not standard K at fixed T.

Adding inert gas at fixed total pressure differs from adding it at fixed volume.

::: {.notes}
Use a delta-nu-nonzero case and explain dilution. Lab 12 is fixed-pressure; do not extrapolate its inert response to a rigid vessel.
:::

## Class demonstration · Lab 12

[Open chemical equilibrium](labs/reaction.html#rx-experiment)

1. Compare all applicable routes at the synthetic reference T.
2. Change T and compare ΔCp and constant-property results.
3. Change pressure at fixed T; inspect extent and atom balances.
4. Export the study and restore it to repeat the calculation.

::: {.notes}
25 minutes. Show the Q equilibrium assertion only after explaining the logical distinction. Avoid implying that clicking a checkbox proves equilibrium.
:::

## Guided exploration · 35 minutes

Choose one temperature change and one pressure change.

Keep a table of lnK, Q, reaction direction and equilibrium extent. Explain which quantities change for each intervention.

Independently check one atom balance and one H−TS or van ’t Hoff calculation.

::: {.notes}
Use source defaults for a reproducible first comparison. Groups that finish early can perturb Kref and diagnose inconsistent anchors.
:::

## Reaction scaling changes K

Reversing the reaction changes lnK to −lnK. Multiplying every coefficient by c changes lnK to c lnK.

Formation sums, reaction H, S, Cp and direct ΔG must transform on the same basis.

A numerical K without a written reaction is incomplete information.

::: {.notes}
Prepare the connection to electrochemistry: n scales too, so E can remain invariant even though K changes.
:::

## Exit question

At the same temperature, pressure increases and equilibrium conversion changes.

Does this mean the equilibrium constant changed?

What additional information is needed before using one ΔG° value at a second temperature?

::: {.notes}
Expected distinction between standard K and Q/composition; need H/S/Cp or justified temperature law. Same standard states and reaction basis remain essential.
:::

## Independent practice · suggested 60–90 minutes

Compare constant-property and heat-capacity routes; report ln K, Q and one extent/material-balance check.

Retain the calculator export, your worksheet, a comparison plot/table and one independent check. State an assumption that limits your conclusion.

Use the core labs on the [learning path](labs/learning-path.html#session-5). Optional extensions are additional work.
